rounds.text: Menon Bearings is demonstrating exceptional operating performance, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 90% [E17] and sales growth of 41% [E15]. The company generates elite returns, boasting a return on capital employed (ROCE) of 23.81% against a sector benchmark of 12.77% [E10], alongside an impressive return on equity (ROE) of 20.64% [E9]. Furthermore, institutional participation is strengthening with positive money flow and domestic institutional holdings rising to 2.16% by September 2026 [E37, E38]. Growth visibility is exceptionally robust, supported by a targeted 25% to 30% capacity expansion in bearings funded entirely through internal accruals [E76, E84], alongside a burgeoning active request-for-quotation (RFQ) list of about ₹75 crores across the aluminium and bi-metal segments [E83]. Management is aggressively scaling high-potential growth verticals, targeting ₹100 crores for Alkop this year [E90], expanding the railway brake segment toward ₹30 crores within two years [E92], and unlocking substantial volume additions from recent international visits to Canada and USA [E73]. Conceded: the stock trades at a rich valuation with a price-to-book ratio of 7.04x [E2] and a discounted cash flow model pointing to overvaluation [E62], but these multiples are fully justified by elite operational efficiency and accelerating top-line momentum.

The market price of ₹252 rests on a severe valuation disconnect supported neither by fundamental cash flows nor conservative book metrics [E2, E39]. A discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of ₹147 per share, exposing a massive margin of safety deficit of -71.9% [E39, E40]. Furthermore, the current market price implies an aggressive 12.4% earnings growth rate, which starkly outpaces the 5.0% baseline projection [E41]. Trading at a lofty price-to-book ratio of 7.04x relative to a sector benchmark of 2.54x, the equity is aggressively priced for perfection [E2, E7]. Compounded profit growth over a three-year period stands at a modest 5%, highlighting a glaring divergence between long-term earnings expansion and runaway price appreciation [E16]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing twelve-month profit growth of 90% alongside healthy returns on capital employed [E10, E17]. However, this cyclical momentum coincides with a concerning retreat in insider confidence, as promoter holdings have declined to 66.65% from 70.18% [E35, E52].

The bear relies heavily on the discounted cash flow model of ₹147 per share and a -71.9% margin of safety [E39, E40], but static DCF outputs ignore explosive near-term catalysts, such as TTM sales growth hitting 41% and TTM profit growth surging by 90% [E15, E17]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is elevated at 7.04x versus the sector benchmark of 2.54x [E2, E7], yet this premium is justified by an exceptional ROE of 20.64% and ROCE of 23.81%, heavily outperforming sector benchmarks of 11.57% and 12.77% [E9, E10]. The bear cites a modest 5% three-year profit growth [E16], but overlooks a massive active RFQ list of about ₹75 crores across aluminium and bi-metal segments, alongside Alkop revenue targets of ₹100 crores this year and ₹125 crores next year [E71, E83]. While promoter holdings decreased to 66.65% [E35], this minor reduction is entirely overshadowed by institutional money flow registering as POSITIVE MONEY FLOW with domestic institutions increasing their stake to 2.16% [E37, E38]. Furthermore, the bear's concern over stretched pricing ignoring fundamentals [E2, E39] ignores the company's aggressive capacity expansions, including a ₹9 crore to ₹10 crore investment lifting bearing capacity by up to 30% to generate over ₹25 crores in new revenue [E76].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales grew by 41% and profit growth surged by 90% [E15, E17], and the company maintains an active RFQ list of about ₹75 crores alongside Alkop targets [E71, E83]. However, citing these near-term figures ignores the fundamental warning of the reverse DCF, which proves that today's price already demands a sustained 12.4% earnings growth compared to the baseline 5.0% assumption [E41]. While the bull points to strong returns on capital and equity [E9, E10], these metrics fail to justify trading at a severe premium of 7.04x to 8.12x book value against a sector benchmark of just 2.54x [E2, E7]. The bull's dismissal of declining promoter ownership [E35] as a minor reduction ignores the clear negative signal of insider selling, while domestic institutional inflows of 2.16% [E37] remain minuscule compared to the broader structural drop in total promoter confidence over time [E35]. Furthermore, the bull leans heavily on planned capacity expansions [E76], but ignores the reality that borrowings actually ticked upward to ₹49 crores in September 2026 [E33] while cash conversion remains only moderate at 0.61x [E28].

Conceded: a reverse DCF implies a 12.4% growth rate against a 5.0% base case [E41], and borrowings ticked upward to ₹49 crores [E33]. However, that rich valuation is fully backed by elite fundamental quality, evidenced by an ROE of 20.64% and ROCE of 23.81% that comprehensively dwarf sector benchmarks of 11.57% and 12.77% [E9, E10]. The bear highlights the high price-to-book multiple of 7.04x to 8.12x [E2, E7], but ignores that this premium reflects superior operational efficiency, demonstrated by a stellar 16.42% ROA compared to the sector benchmark of just 6.48% [E8]. Conceded: promoters hold slightly less at 66.65% [E35], but this reduction is offset by positive institutional money flow (+1.83 percentage points) driven by domestic inflows reaching 2.16% [E37, E38]. Finally, while cash conversion is noted at 0.61x [E28], the company generated ₹23 crores in operating cash flow and maintains a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.51x, funding its expansions entirely through internal accruals rather than burdensome new debt [E29, E32, E84].

Conceded: ROE of 20.64% and ROCE of 23.81% comprehensively dwarf sector benchmarks of 11.57% and 12.77% [E9, E10], and the company maintains a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.51x [E32]. However, pointing to elite fundamentals like a 16.42% ROA [E8] does not neutralize the severe warning that a discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at just ₹147 per share against a market price of ₹252, resulting in an alarming margin of safety of -71.9% [E39, E40]. Conceded: domestic institutions increased holdings to 2.16% [E37] and institutional money flow shows positive movement [E38], but this minor institutional accumulation occurred while total promoter holding actively declined from 70.18% to 66.65% [E35]. Furthermore, while the bull celebrates funding expansions through internal accruals [E84], total borrowings actually ticked upward to ₹49 crores in September 2026 from ₹47 crores a year earlier [E33]. Finally, a price-to-book multiple of 7.04x to 8.12x [E2, E7] alongside a reverse DCF implying 12.4% earnings growth [E41] proves that the stock's performance is entirely price-led with expectations running far ahead of delivery [E51].

evidence.quote: The total potential of additional business for the current and next financial year is expected to be around INR65 crores to INR75 crores, subject to good monsoon and geopolitical situation doesn't worsen further.

evidence.fact: The company expects business in the railway brake segment to start with INR5 crores to INR6 crores and grow to INR25 crores to INR30 crores within two years.
evidence.quote: with this in the first year itself, we expect that to start with, we will have a business of around INR5 crores to INR6 crores to start with and eventually it will go up to INR25 crores to INR30 crores within next two years.

evidence.fact: The company is targeting revenues of INR100 crores for Alkop this year and around INR125 crores next year.
evidence.quote: For this year, we are targeting Alkop for INR100 crores, next year around INR125 crores.

evidence.fact: The underlying demand outlook for the automotive and engineering sector remains encouraging despite global uncertainties.
evidence.quote: While the global business environment continues to present certain uncertainties, the underlying demand outlook for the automotive and engineering sector remains encouraging.

evidence.fact: The management's visit to Canada and USA is expected to yield substantial volume additions in the coming period of the year.
evidence.quote: That is because, more particularly, due to our last month's visit to Canada and USA, is expected to yield substantial volumes in the coming period of the year.

evidence.fact: Potential revenue from Africa is estimated at around INR9 crores for bearings, bushes, and washers, and INR6 crores to INR7 crores for brake linings.
evidence.quote: You see the possible revenue from Africa so far as bearing, bushes and washers are concerned is around INR9 crores. And at the same time, we are working on supplies to Africa so far as brake linings are concerned, and that is expected to be around INR6 crores to INR7 crores for the year.

evidence.fact: The dynamometer machine for the brake segment is under construction and expected by the end of August.
evidence.quote: You see, basically that is under construction now and is expected by the end of August.

evidence.fact: The company is investing INR9 crores to INR10 crores this financial year to increase bearing capacity by 25% to 30%.
evidence.quote: If you go through the presentation, Rucheeta, you will come to know that we are investing about INR9 crores to INR10 crores of rupees for this year, this financial year for increasing the capacity and which is expected to increase the capacity by almost 25% to 30%, which may yield the total revenue of more than INR25 crores, which can generate revenue of INR25 crores.

evidence.fact: The company is executing a CapEx of around INR4 crores for the current year in the Alkop division alone.
evidence.quote: And we are having the CapEx of around INR4 crores of for this year in Alkop alone.

evidence.fact: Consolidated EBITDA grew by 57% during Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: And EBITDA on a consolidated basis is up by 57%.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margin in the brake segment increased to 25% in the current quarter.
evidence.quote: But at the same time, I would like to tell you that right from 12% EBITDA earlier, now we have reached to 25% EBITDA in brakes also.

evidence.fact: Average raw material prices for aluminium increased to INR340-370, driving realisation above INR900.
evidence.quote: Otherwise, it is roughly around when it is INR250 rupees or INR200 aluminium, it is around INR700. But now average aluminium rates have become INR340, INR370.

evidence.fact: Standalone sales for Bi-metal Menon Bearings grew 40.41% year-on-year to INR67.06 crores during Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: Now coming to the standalone performance of Bi-metal Menon Bearings, during the quarter sales increased to INR67.06 crores from INR47.76 crores as compared to the corresponding quarter of the last year that is year-on-year increase of 40.41% and further increased by about 41%.

evidence.fact: The bi-metal bearing segment has a potential peak revenue capacity above INR400 crores.
evidence.quote: Peak revenue from this, it can be aboveINR400 crores.

evidence.quote: So, put together, Alkop, that is Aluminium and Bi-metal put together, the list of such RFQ list is about INR75 crores of rupees apart from the potential business that we may get through our visits to Canada and USA, that is different.

evidence.fact: Planned investments for the bi-metal and Alkop segments will be funded entirely through internal accruals without new debt.
evidence.quote: You see, so far as whatever we are considering so far as bi-metal and Alkop is concerned, it will be through internal accruals only, no fresh loan will be taken.
